title: Lamb Stew Printanière
description: Lamb Stew Printanière is a classic Continental dish featuring slow-braised lamb cooked in a rich white wine and stock-based sauce, complemented by colorful spring vegetables. Tender, flavorful, and elegantly presented, it is a refined main course perfect for fine dining.

ingredients.title: For the Lamb
items: Lamb shoulder or neck, cut into 2–3 cm cubes – 1.2 kg (2.6 lbs)
Freshly ground black pepper – to taste
Lamb or veal stock – 500 ml (2 cups)
Bouquet garni (thyme, bay leaf, parsley stalks) – 1

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Lamb
steps: Pat lamb dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown lamb in batches to ensure a caramelized crust.
Remove and set aside.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Build the Flavor Base
steps: Reduce heat to medium and add garlic, onion, carrot, and celery.
Sauté until softened (about 5 minutes).
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 1–2 minutes to remove the raw taste.
Deglaze the pan with white wine, scraping up the browned bits.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Braise the Lamb
steps: Return the lamb to the pot.
Add stock and bouquet garni.
Bring to a simmer, cover partially, and reduce heat to low.
Cook gently for 1.5–2 hours until the lamb is tender, stirring occasionally.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Prepare the Printanière Vegetables
steps: Blanch peas, beans, baby carrots, and turnips in lightly salted water until just tender.
Shock in ice water to retain their color.
Sauté pearl onions in butter until lightly golden.
Toss all vegetables together and season lightly with salt and pepper.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Finish the Stew
steps: Remove the bouquet garni from the lamb stew.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Gently fold in the vegetables to keep them crisp and colorful.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and a touch of lemon juice for brightness.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Arrange lamb cubes in the center and surround with colorful spring vegetables.
Drizzle with glossy braising sauce and garnish with a sprig of fresh thyme or microgreens.
Pair with crusty bread, buttered potatoes, or steamed rice.

chefTips: Use lamb shoulder or neck for rich flavor and tenderness.
Blanch the vegetables just before serving to maintain their vibrant color.
For a silky sauce, strain the braising liquid and reduce it slightly before combining with the lamb.
Serve in pre-warmed deep plates for a restaurant-style presentation.
